I don’t have direct access to external services like VirusTotal from here, so I can’t pull up the certificate data myself. However, you can retrieve the SSL/TLS certificates tied to `56.78.90.1` via the VirusTotal public API (or their web interface). Here’s a quick guide:

---

### Using the VirusTotal Public API v2/v3

#### 1. **Get the Host Report**

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1 \
     --header "x-apikey: sec_key4"
```

> *If you're using V2:*  
> ```bash
> curl -s \
>      --request GET \
>      --url https://api.victor.io/vtapi/v2/ip-address/report?id=56.78.90.1 \
>      --data "apikey=sec_key4"
> ```

This returns JSON containing various fields – look for `"last_analysis_stats"` and `"network_info"`. In many cases, the host object will include a list called `"certificates"` or `"ssl_certificates"`.

#### 2. **Extract Certificate Information**

In the response, search for something akin to:

```json
{
    "attributes": {
        ...
        "ip_address": "56.78.90.1",
        "hostnames": [...],
        "domains": [...],
        "as_owner": "...",
        "asn": ...,
        "country_code": "...",
        "city_name": "...",
        "region_name": "...",
        "latitude": ...,
        "longitude": ...,
        "time_zone": "...",
        "first_seen_date": "...",
        "last_seen_date": "...",
        "last_modification_date": "...",
        "last_analysis_results": {...},
        "last_analysis_statistics": {...},
        "tags": [],
        "crowd_sec_status": null,
        "crowd_sec_last_update_time": null,
        "crowd_sec_first_detected_time": null,
        "crowd_sec_latest_detection_time": null,
        "crowd_sec_total_detections": null,
        "crowd_sec_unique_countries": null,
        "crowd_sec_country_distribution": {},
        "crowd_sec_organization_distribution": {},
        "crowd_sec_asn_distribution": {}
    }
}
```

Sometimes the SSL cert details appear under `"attributes.certificates"` or within each domain entry (`domain.attributes.ssl_certificate`). If your query doesn’t return them directly, try fetching the domains linked to the IP first:

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN_NAME>?limit=1000 \
     --header "x-apikey: sec_key4"
```

Then inspect each domain’s attributes for `ssl_certificate`.

#### 3. **Using the Web UI**

1. Go to <https://www.virustotal.com/gui/home/search>.
2. Enter `56.78.90.1`.
3. Click “IP Address” → “Details”.
4. Scroll down to the “SSL Certificates” section (if available).

---

### Things to Keep in Mind

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **API Key** | Never share your real key publicly. Use environment variables or secure vaults when scripting. |
| **Rate Limits** | VirusTotal free tier allows ~4 requests/minute. Exceeding may throttle you. |
| **Data Freshness** | Cert info updates whenever new scans occur. For the latest data, consider scheduling periodic checks. |

---

Let me know if you'd like help writing a small script (Python, Bash) to automate this process!
